title: Senator Doug Mastriano highlights Homestead Act anniversary and local updates in Adams County
text:
Pennsylvania State Senator Doug Mastriano, who represents Adams and Franklin counties and has chaired the Senate Veterans Affairs and Emergency Preparedness Committee, posted a series of updates on his social media account on May 20, 2026. The posts covered historical reflection, local infrastructure news, and outreach to constituents.
On May 20, Mastriano marked the anniversary of a significant moment in U.S. history, writing: “May 20th, 1862 – President Abraham Lincoln signed the Homestead Act into law. This act granted U.S. citizens or future citizens up to 160 acres of public land, provided they lived on and improved it for a specified period. The Homestead Act was a major factor in the westward https://t.co/RBHDwdFrhs” (posted at 12:00 UTC).
Later that day, he informed residents about upcoming road work in Adams County: ” Road Work Alert – Adams County
 May 26–29 7:00 AM – 3:00 PM (weather permitting)
 Expect https://t.co/VD9E7XgHnr” (posted at 18:46 UTC).
In an evening post, Mastriano encouraged constituents to subscribe to his weekly newsletter: “Don’t miss out! Discover valuable insights in my weekly newsletter, delivered every Friday. Sign up now for exclusive content! https://t.co/ZY1JT0dDQA” (posted at 22:00 UTC).
Senator Mastriano’s legislative efforts have emphasized veteran support and community service initiatives through both policy and direct engagement with residents (official website). He has operated within state governance as a representative and has led committees focused on veterans affairs and local government matters. His communications reflect ongoing engagement with local issues such as infrastructure projects affecting Adams County.
